maya: Heads up — after pushing runtime v7.3.1 to canary (5% cohort) we saw a p95+p99 jump for a paying tenant (Acme). baseline p95 ~82ms -> canary p95 ~205ms, p99 from 210ms -> 770ms. noticed ~2026-03-17T10:02 UTC when traffic hit.

oliver: Ugh. Can you paste the canary cohort id and a couple trace ids? Any errors or 429s?

maya: cohort=canary-2026-03-17-5pct. No 429s, no obvious 5xx. Sample traces: trace/4c3b2a, trace/8f9d01. Putting top-level metrics below.

maya: ```metrics
metric.p95=82ms (stable) -> 205ms (canary)
metric.p99=210ms -> 770ms
req_rate ~ stable
queue_depth tails increased on 3 hosts
io_wait% on affected hosts spiked from ~1% -> ~18%
```

elena: That iowait number stands out. Which hosts are in the canary cohort? Any newer kernel or kernel-scheduler changes in this rollout?

maya: canary hosts: r-host-12-15, r-host-18. Runtime image tag: runtime:v7.3.1+patch. Deploy bot shows node image includes kernel-sched bump from r2345.

deploy-bot: deployment runtime:v7.3.1 rolled to 20 pods across hosts [r-host-12..r-host-19] at 2026-03-17T09:58Z.

samir: Quick hypothesis: scheduler change increased context switches causing NVMe/disk IO scheduling jitter that impacts our KV cache persistence/eviction path -> more kmsyncs, more io_wait under certain request patterns. Seen similar when batching aligns badly.

liz: Any change in batching config? Did we accidentally enable larger max_batch for HTTPS ingress?

maya: No batching config change in this rollout. Only runtime binary + kernel-sched bump.

oliver: Let's bisect the candidate set: (A) kernel-sched r2345, (B) runtime allocator tweak r2370, (C) minor logging flush change r2399. We should repro locally with a small A/B harness hitting a hot prefix cohort.

elena: I'll run iostat + pidstat on r-host-12 while we replay traffic.

maya: Repro steps I used (short):
```bash
# from perf box
./loadgen --target https://canary-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  --clients 20 --requests 10000 --prompt-file samples/hot_prefix.txt \
  --headers 'Authorization: Bearer $CANARY_KEY' --concurrency 8
```
I observed p95 jump within 90s.

oliver: Good. I'll spin up a two-host canary mirror with v7.3.0 vs v7.3.1 and run that load. Can you capture `perf record -F 99 -p <pid>` and `pprof` snapshots? Also get `vmstat 1` and `iostat -x 1` during the run.

elena: initial quick captures:
```
# r-host-12 (v7.3.1)
%user 2.4 %system 3.1 %iowait 17.8 ctxt/vol 18500
# r-host-14 (v7.3.0)
%user 2.2 %system 3.0 %iowait 1.2 ctxt/vol 4200
```

elena: pidstat shows runtime process blocked on synchronous fd writes in the async persistence path — many short written batches, fsyncs aligned with batching boundaries.

samir: That matches the scheduler influence on IO bursts. If the scheduler groups threads differently, we can see batch flush times align causing NVMe queue saturation.

oliver: I ran A/B mirror ramp; confirmed: v7.3.1 host shows p99 ~760ms, v7.3.0 host p99 ~215ms. Flamegraphs show increased time in persistence flush syscall on v7.3.1. Link: https://perf.redwood.ai/flame/trace/4c3b2a (internal).

maya: Customer impacted (Acme) support ticket #RWD-4582 opened. Support already notified.

support-bot: Notified account team + customer success. Customer currently seeing latency spikes on their gen endpoint.

liz: Mitigation options: 1) immediate rollback of kernel-sched on canary hosts, 2) route Acme traffic to stable pool, 3) temporary throttle batch flush frequency (if quick config toggle available), 4) pin canary cohort to hosts without kernel bump. Which is fastest?

oliver: Fastest is to pin traffic for that tenant to stable pool (route policy) and rollback canary on affected hosts if we want to stop further noise. I'll open a rollback PR.

maya: I've applied traffic pin for Acme to stable via routing rule (confirmed). Observed p95 for Acme drop back to ~90ms within 45s.

deploy-bot: routing rule applied: route tenant=acme -> pool=stable-1 at 2026-03-17T10:12Z.

elena: I'll start a controlled rollback of kernel-sched on the 3 affected hosts and keep the runtime image same. Rolling one host now.

oliver: Parallel action: start bisect on infra side. We'll repro with kernel-sched toggled on/off to confirm root cause. If confirmed, mark r2345 as revert candidate. Also file infra ticket INFRA-7832.

maya: Quick notes for the postmortem: reproduce steps (above), artifacts: perf recordings (s3://perf/artifacts/1722500000/), iostat vmstat logs, A/B mirror results, routing rule applied, rollback timeline.

samir: Long-term fix possibilities: adjust async persistence flush to be jittered (avoid alignment), add backpressure for NVMe queue, or change scheduler paramization. Also add a canary smoke test for iowait-sensitive patterns.

liz: Customer comms: CS drafted a note explaining we routed them to stable and we're investigating; ETA for root cause tomorrow EOD.

maya: Action items: oliver -> bisect + revert PR if confirmed; elena -> finish rollback of kernel-sched on canary hosts and gather logs; samir -> design jittered flush PoC; liz -> own customer comms.

oliver: I'll update this thread when bisect completes. Thanks all :thumbsup:
